idiom_name: Option combinators (map / and_then / filter) with Iterator::filter_map / flat_map
implementation_notes: Option<T> is a core sum type and the 0..1 focus: map transforms a present value, and_then chains a step that itself returns Option (the documentation notes that some languages call this operation flatmap), and filter drops a value that fails a predicate, while the ? operator propagates None out of a function. The plural traversal is the Iterator combinators - filter_map both filters and maps with one closure, flat_map flattens nested iterables - and Option itself is iterable (Some yields one item, None yields none), so a chain of adapters is the traversal. These replace the classic optic structure; a hand-written loop is still right when a single pass suffices.
pitfalls: Iterator chains are lazy: a pipeline that is never consumed does nothing, and collect consumes the iterator, so a second pass needs the chain rebuilt.
unwrap/expect panic on None; unwrap_or, map_or or the ? operator keep the absent case explicit.
and_then expects a closure returning Option while map expects a plain value; mixing them yields Option<Option<T>> instead of flattening.
